The name Gamergate was patterned after Watergate and is a movement wanting ethics and accountability in the journalism in games media. One of the big difficulties that games journalists have is needing to be in the good graces of developers and publishers, big and small, in order to get early game copies to review in a timely fashion. If they are not in their good graces, they won't get early copies. They will then have to resort to getting their copy on release day, then rush through and attempt to publish a review as soon after the release day as they can. They will automatically lose traffic that way because people want to read reviews before the game comes out.

Another one of the big difficulties is that advertising space on their websites are predominantly purchased by game developers and game publishers. Not a lot of other companies buy advertising space on gaming websites. That puts the games journalists in a difficult position where they are giving reviews on products sold by the very same companies that pay their bills. Combine that with some unethical people in said company's marketing teams who will put pressure on the games journalists to give the games positive reviews or be blacklisted and you have a precarious position for the games journalists. Therefore both the ethics and appearance of ethics of games journalists become extremely important but have been severely lacking.

I'm not sure if this has been submitted before, a quick search brought up nothing, but I have no doubt it probably has.

That said, the submission quota or "timer" per hour is honestly prohibitive to getting content on smaller subs.

I run /v/MMA and there are times when there is a ton of news missing and I'm unable to submit it because the obnoxiously low quota prevents me from linking more than a few things and starting up our regular discussion threads while I'm active. This forces me to keep a bunch of tabs open and wait for an hour each time before submitting a batch of content, which makes submission more of a job than anything.

I propose that in the interest of growing voat, we lift or raise these restrictions as they are pretty much unnecessary. At best they would prevent spammers, but realistically it's the job of the mods and users to control that via content removal and potential bans for repeat offenders and downvoating spam content, respectively.

At worst they are preventing some of the more active posts from contributing content everyone else wants and supports at the expense of protecting us from.... nothing.

If it cannot be removed, at the very least, please allow the founders/mods of subs to have differing restrictions or allow us some level of granular control over what our subs limits are. Maybe give us the ability to raise it to a max of X per hour... say maybe 10 as the max?

At the very least, I hope it is considered, because right now it's stifling.
